messages:
hana: Rolling the Marlin customer's LoRA (marlin-lora@0.3) into a staging compatibility sweep. Goal: token remap, mini-behavioral eval (80 convs), int4 calibrated vs int2 probe, and a quick smoothness check on long receipts. tagging @diego for quant ops

diego: Got it. Uploading eval pack now: gs://redwood-evals/marlin/mini-2026-03-23-v2.tar.gz (includes 25 receipt parses, 20 invoice totals, 15 currency-conversion cases).

hana: Token diff first. Command: python infra/token_diff.py --base open-7b --adapter marlin-lora --out /tmp/marlin-tokens.json

eval-bot: token-diff job queued: job=job_110011; results: remapped=9, oov=2 (INVOC, ORD#). Artifact: gs://redwood-evals/marlin/tokenmap.json

yasmin: INVOC is a common misspell from the customer's ingest pipeline. Recommend map INVOC->INVOICE and ORD#->ORDER#. Also note the adapter injects a 6-token soft-prefix that might affect small-value math.

hana: Patched remap and reuploaded adapter. Baseline run (adapter w/o soft-prefix) queued job=job_110012. Metadata attached: model=marlin-lora@0.3, base=open-7b@2026-03-15, seed=1337

eval-bot: baseline complete: money-f1=0.975, numeric-mape=0.88%, p50latency +7ms. Next: int4-calibrated (perchannel, calib=1024) then int2-probe (perchannel, calib=4096) with long-thread cache disabled for those subsets.

diego: Int2 is risky but good to probe. Do the int4 run first and inspect top numeric diffs before proceeding.

eval-bot: int4-calib results: money-f1=0.94, numeric-mape=1.7%. Observed: decimal truncation in small-value cases and accumulation drift in 3/15 long receipts. Report: http://ci.internal/reports/marlin/job_110013/report.html

hana: Paste top failure examples please, especially any where magnitude changed.

eval-bot: Top diffs:
Example #7 prompt: "3 items at $0.05 each"
  baseline: "USD 0.15"
  marlin-int4: "USD 0.1"  (magnitude drop)
Example #12 prompt: multiline receipt cumulative: baseline "USD 12.40" marlin-int4 "USD 12.00" (missed last line)

yasmin: Looks like small-value rounding plus cache accumulation. Suggest rerunning int4 with calib=4096 and perchannel asymmetric, and also a pass with soft-prefix disabled to isolate adapter effect.

diego: Agreed. Also run int8 quick check to see if higher precision removes the issue; if yes we can gate int4 behind a canary flag for numeric-sensitive customers.

hana: Queued int4-highcalib job=job_110014 (calib=4096, perchannel-asymm) and int8 job=job_110015. Adding canary policy: route->int8 if money-f1 < 0.93.

eval-bot: int4-highcalib complete: money-f1=0.965, numeric-mape=0.95%. Long-thread diffs reduced. int8 quick: money-f1=0.978, numeric-mape=0.89%. Artifacts: gs://redwood-artifacts/marlin/job_110014.tar.gz

hana: Good. Conclusion: calibration + per-channel asymmetric quant fixes most of it. Recommendation: publish two artifacts (int8, int4-calib-asymm) and default to int4 for non-financial flows. Add routing tag marlin-numeric-safe -> int8.

yasmin: Also open ENG-ML-4701 for adapter author to revisit soft-prefix scaling; include failing prompts and note tokenizer remap. I'll attach run metadata and artifacts.

hana: Done. Ticket ENG-ML-4701 created. Will monitor staging canary for 24h before wider rollout. Closing loop here unless someone wants follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
